title: 4 Nights in Nantucket — A Foodie & Relaxation Itinerary for Two: Seafood, Beaches & Golden Sunsets
description: A personalized 4-night Nantucket itinerary for a couple — lobster rolls, oyster bars, Madaket sunsets, beach days, bike rides to Sconset, and Cisco Brewers. Late May perfection.

days.title: Arrive, Wander the Cobblestones & First Oysters
days.description: You're on an island 30 miles out to sea. The moment the ferry pulls into the harbor and you see the grey-shingled rooftops and the Brant Point Lighthouse, something shifts. Today is about settling in, exploring the town on foot, and eating your first lobster roll.

activities.name: Ferry to Nantucket
activities.description: Take the Hy-Line High-Speed Ferry from Hyannis (~1 hour, ~$45/person one-way) or the Steamship Authority fast ferry (~1 hour). As you pull into the harbor, watch for Brant Point Lighthouse on the left — it's the second-oldest lighthouse in America and your first "we're really here" moment. Drop your bags at your accommodation and head straight into town. Everything in Nantucket Town is walkable.

activities.name: Cobblestone Main Street & Whaling Museum
activities.description: Stroll up Main Street — the wide cobblestone avenue lined with elm trees, brick storefronts, and galleries. This is the heart of Nantucket and it looks like it hasn't changed in 200 years (because it mostly hasn't). Browse the boutiques, peek into art galleries, grab a coffee. Visit the Whaling Museum — a beautifully curated museum in a former candle factory that tells the story of Nantucket's whaling era. The 46-foot sperm whale skeleton suspended from the ceiling is jaw-dropping. The rooftop observation deck has panoramic views of the harbor and town.

activities.name: Walk to Brant Point Lighthouse
activities.description: A 15-minute walk from town along the harbor to Nantucket's most iconic landmark. The lighthouse is small but photogenic, and the little beach next to it is a perfect spot to sit and watch the ferries come in. Throw a penny in the water on your way off the island (tradition says it guarantees your return).

days.neighborhoods: Surfside Beach · Cisco Brewers · Bartlett's Farm
days.title: Beach Morning, Farm Stand & Craft Brewery Afternoon
days.description: Today is the perfect Nantucket day — morning at the beach, a stop at the island's legendary farm stand, and an afternoon at Cisco Brewers with live music and cold drinks in the sun. This is island time at its finest.

activities.name: Surfside Beach
activities.description: Nantucket's most popular beach, and for good reason — wide sandy shore, good waves, and a classic beach shack for snacks. It's a 15-minute bike ride from town (flat, paved bike path the whole way) or take the NRTA shuttle. In late May the crowds are still manageable. Bring a blanket, sunscreen, and the sandwiches from Something Natural. The water will be brisk (~59°F/15°C) but the brave take a dip. The beach itself is beautiful even just for lounging and listening to the waves.

activities.name: Bartlett's Farm
activities.description: The island's oldest and largest farm — a gorgeous farm stand with fresh produce, prepared foods, flowers, baked goods, and everything you need for a picnic. Grab some local cheeses, fresh bread, and whatever looks good. Even if you don't buy much, it's a beautiful stop and a reminder that this island grows its own food.

activities.name: Cisco Brewers
activities.description: This is not just a brewery — it's a whole campus. Cisco Brewers (craft beer), Triple Eight Distillery (vodka, gin, whiskey), and Nantucket Vineyard (wine) all share one sprawling outdoor space with picnic tables, food trucks, and live music most afternoons. It's the island's unofficial gathering place. Order a flight of Cisco beers (the Whale's Tale Pale Ale is the classic), try a cocktail with Triple Eight cranberry vodka, and settle in. The vibe is laid-back, sunny, and perfectly Nantucket. You could easily spend 2–3 hours here without trying.

days.neighborhoods: Milestone Bike Path · 'Sconset Village · Jetties Beach
days.title: Bike to 'Sconset, Rose-Covered Cottages & Jetties Beach
days.description: Today you'll bike across the island to Siasconset ('Sconset) — the tiny village on the eastern shore with rose-covered cottages that looks like a movie set. It's the most charming ride on the island, and the village at the end is worth every pedal stroke.

activities.name: Milestone Bike Path to 'Sconset
activities.description: Rent bikes and take the Milestone Road Bike Path — a flat, paved, dedicated cycling path that runs 6.5 miles from town to 'Sconset. The ride takes about 40–50 minutes at a leisurely pace, passing through moors, grasslands, and the occasional pond. It's one of the most scenic bike rides in New England. The path is well-maintained, flat (Nantucket has essentially no hills), and separated from car traffic. Pack water and sunscreen.

activities.name: Siasconset ('Sconset)
activities.description: A tiny village of grey-shingled cottages draped in climbing roses (they'll be just starting to bloom in late May). The village is impossibly charming — narrow lanes, white picket fences, a general store, and a bluff walk with ocean views. Walk the 'Sconset Bluff Walk — a path along the eroding bluff with sweeping views of the Atlantic. It's short but stunning. The 'Sconset Casino (not a gambling casino — it's a tennis and cultural club from the 1800s) hosts movies and events in summer. The building itself is beautiful.

activities.name: Jetties Beach
activities.description: Bike back to town (or take the shuttle) and spend the afternoon at Jetties Beach — the closest beach to town, with calm waters, a playground, and a beach bar. It's more sheltered than Surfside, making it perfect for a mellow afternoon. The Jetties Beach Bistro serves drinks and food right on the sand.

activities.name: White Elephant Spa
activities.description: Treat yourselves to a couples massage or treatment at the White Elephant Resort spa. It's one of the island's premier spas — serene, beautifully appointed, with harbor views. Book a 60-minute couples massage to recover from the bike ride. Pure indulgence.

days.title: Lazy Beach Day & the Best Sunset You've Ever Seen
days.description: Your last full day. No agenda, no rushing. A beach, some tacos, and the legendary Madaket sunset. This is the day you'll remember most.

activities.name: Cisco Beach
activities.description: The locals' beach. Wider, wilder, and less crowded than Surfside. Great waves, big sky, and a raw Atlantic energy. Spread out your blanket, read a book, nap in the sun. This is the kind of beach day that recharges your soul. You're 10 minutes by bike from Cisco Brewers if you need a mid-day drink.

activities.name: Madaket Beach — Sunset
activities.description: This is the main event. Madaket Beach faces due west and has what many consider the most spectacular sunset on the East Coast. The sky turns every shade of pink, orange, and purple as the sun drops into the ocean. It's a 20-minute bike ride or shuttle from town — take the Madaket Bike Path (flat, beautiful, 5.5 miles). Arrive at least an hour before sunset to grab a good spot. Bring a blanket and a bottle of wine. Watch the sky change. This is the kind of moment that makes a trip.

days.title: One Last Morning Walk, Then Home
days.description: A gentle final morning. Soak in the last of the island before catching the ferry back to the mainland. No rush — just one more walk, one more coffee, one more look at those cobblestones.

activities.name: Morning Stroll Through Town
activities.description: Take one final walk through the cobblestone streets. Wander down Centre Street and India Street, peek into the shops you missed, and grab any last-minute souvenirs. Pick up saltwater taffy, Nantucket-themed goods, or a jar of beach plum jam from one of the specialty shops. Walk back to Brant Point Lighthouse one more time. Throw your penny in the harbor. You'll be back.

activities.name: Ferry Back to Hyannis
activities.description: Head to the Steamship Authority or Hy-Line dock for your ferry back. Grab a seat on the upper deck for one last look at the island as it shrinks into the ocean behind you. The hour-long ride is a nice decompression before heading home.
